B: Hiya! Oh, hello! Greta, is it?
A: Yes. Hi. And you're Leanne.
B: That's me, Castleford. You're Peterborough? I've been through on the train to London, never got off, sorry.
A: That's what most people do. Don't worry.
B: Ha! So what do you do?
A: Graphic design. At a print company. Leaflets, menus, vans.
B: Ooh, that's clever. I'm on a packing line at a food factory, so a bit different. Is that your work behind you, them pictures?
A: Lino prints, yes. I make them at home. That one is a fish, the other is rooftops.
B: They're lovely. I wouldn't know where to start. Do you carve them out yourself?
A: Yes, with little knives, backwards, because it prints the other way round. Erm, I cut my thumb a lot.
B: Backwards! See, I'd mess that up straight away. I do cakes, that's my arty thing. Birthday cakes, traybakes for work. I did a Tigers one for my nephew, the rugby, black and amber.
A: Cake is design too, to be honest. Colour, shape, you have to plan.
B: Aw, I've never thought of it like that! I'll tell them at work I'm a designer now. Ha.
A: Please do. It's more design than half the things my boss approves.
B: Oh dear, is he a bit, you know?
A: He likes everything big and red. Every client, big and red.
B: Ha! Sorry, I shouldn't laugh. So what are you doing for Christmas, you probably think I'm daft asking in October, but our choir's rehearsing already.
A: No, it's fine. I'm Lithuanian, so Christmas Eve is the big one. Kūčios. Twelve dishes, no meat. My mum rings on video to check I really did twelve.
B: Twelve! What, like a buffet?
A: Sort of. Herring, mushrooms, beetroot, little poppy seed biscuits in milk. Some I only make because she watches. And I go to the Lithuanian Mass at Christmas, maybe Easter.
B: Oh, that's nice. I'm at chapel, Methodist, mostly for the singing to be honest. We do a big Christmas concert there. I'd cry if I tried twelve dishes, I can barely do a shepherd's pie.
A: Twelve is too many, honestly. But if I skip one I feel guilty all year.
B: That's mums for you, isn't it. Even from miles away.
A: Yes. Exactly. From two thousand kilometres.
B: Sorry, I'm rabbiting on. Is the concert poster on my board, did you see? A lady from choir made it.
A: I saw it, yes. Can I be honest?
B: Go on, love.
A: Too many fonts. And I think the date is in Comic Sans.
B: Ha! It is! Oh, Brenda'll be gutted. Would you, erm, I mean, how would you do it then?
A: One font, big date, the chapel name, maybe one small star. Done.
